summary: A Whistler Creative design studio article listing eight tree-free or sustainable paper stocks for print projects, arguing that paper production is heavily linked to forest loss and emissions. Each option is described with its production method, environmental benefits, and suggested uses, from hemp and recycled cotton to seed paper and 100% recycled paper. The page also promotes the studio's services and a March hemp postcard promotion.
one_line: A design studio's guide to eight affordable, tree-free sustainable paper stocks such as hemp, cotton, straw, bamboo, stone, sugarcane, seed and recycled paper.
key_facts: The world consumes around 400 million tons of paper each year, accounting for 70% of global warming according to the article.
Hemp grows to maturity in as little as 90 days, compared to 7 to 35 years for trees.
Regulations against hemp production were recently removed in the USA, making hemp-based paper stocks affordable and readily available.
Recycled cotton paper is typically made from recycled cotton textile scraps such as t-shirts or jeans.
Cotton takes 200 years to biodegrade, according to the article's description of cotton waste in landfill.
The production of straw paper requires 25% less water and 70% less energy than traditional paper.
Stone paper is typically made from calcium carbonate or limestone mixed with high density polyethylene resins (HDPE), and its carbon footprint is almost 60% smaller than traditional papers.
Stone paper can be recycled indefinitely, according to the note.
Bamboo is described as an extremely fast growing grass that can grow almost anywhere, but turning it into paper is still chemically intensive.
Sugarcane (bagasse) paper is made from bagasse, a by-product of the sugarcane plant after it has been harvested for sugar, alcohol juices and biofuel.
Seed paper is embedded with wildflower, herb or vegetable seeds, and the seed blends used are Canada-approved, non-invasive, non-GMO, and safe for planting anywhere in North America.
The article advises that seed paper is best used for digital printing because high heat from some printing methods can damage the seeds' ability to grow.
Recycled paper made from 100% post consumer waste is recommended over virgin fibers, with recycled content typically in quantities of 10%, 30%, 50% or 100%.
Whistler Creative is a Certified Green Graphic Design company with over 15 years experience, according to the note.
The March promotion offers 250 4" x 6" full colour postcards printed on tree-free hemp card stock, with 10% donated to BC Women's Health Foundation.
